description: Batched, single-transaction insert of raw HTTP payloads into raw_games. Called 'upsert' because a re-run of the same acquisition step for the same (run_id, appid, source) key (e.g. a retried failed fetch within the same run) replaces the prior row rather than violating the primary key -- but per ADR-005, this only ever happens within one run's own acquisition pass, never across runs (raw_games rows are immutable once the run's acquisition stage has completed).
signature: def upsert_raw_payloads(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str, payloads: Iterable[RawPayload]) -> int
docstring:
Write a batch of raw payloads.

Args:
    conn: An open connection.
    run_id: The run these payloads belong to.
    payloads: An iterable of RawPayload. Consumed lazily and written in batches (e.g. 500 rows per executemany call) inside one surrounding transaction, so a crash mid-stream leaves the already-committed batches intact per the acquisition invariant 'payloads are persisted in batches as they stream in'.

Returns:
    The number of rows written (post-deduplication if the same (appid, source) appeared twice in payloads, the later one wins).

Raises:
    StorageError: If run_id does not exist, or any payload's payload_sha256 does not match sha256 of its own payload_json serialization (defensive integrity check).
preconditions: each RawPayload.source is one of the four allowed source values
postconditions: After the call, read_raw_payloads(conn, run_id, source) yields every payload written for that source, keyed by (run_id, appid, source)
The whole batch commits atomically per internal sub-batch; the function does not leave a half-written sub-batch uncommitted on success

edge_cases.expected_behavior: writes zero rows, returns 0, does not raise

edge_cases.input: Two RawPayload entries with the same (appid, source) in the same call
edge_cases.expected_behavior: the later one in iteration order wins (INSERT OR REPLACE semantics); both are not written as separate rows since (run_id, appid, source) is the primary key

edge_cases.input: payloads is a generator that raises partway through iteration (e.g. a network error mid-stream from fetch_steamspy_catalog)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: rows from already-completed internal sub-batches remain committed; the exception propagates to the caller after that point, and the return value is never produced (function does not return; it raises)

edge_cases.input: source not in the four allowed values
edge_cases.expected_behavior: StorageError (CHECK constraint violation wrapped) before or during the batch commit

unit_tests.name: test_stores_payloads_byte_equal
unit_tests.description: A payload round-trips through upsert_raw_payloads then read_raw_payloads with byte-identical JSON and matching sha256.
unit_tests.expected: read-back payload_json equals the original bytes; payload_sha256 matches

unit_tests.name: test_empty_iterable_writes_zero
unit_tests.description: An empty list returns 0 and writes nothing.

unit_tests.name: test_duplicate_key_in_batch_last_wins
unit_tests.description: Two payloads for the same appid/source in one call leave only the second's content stored.
unit_tests.expected: one row, matching the second payload's content

unit_tests.name: test_partial_batch_survives_stream_error
unit_tests.description: A generator that yields 600 valid payloads then raises leaves the first committed sub-batch (500) persisted.
unit_tests.expected: 500 rows present after the exception propagates
